key_insight: Microscopic impurities act as degradation nucleation sites in wide-bandgap perovskite films, and machine learning-supported optical imaging can detect and quantify them within seconds.
engineering_relevance: Rapid, non-invasive impurity screening could help prioritize more stable perovskite films for scalable tandem solar-cell manufacturing.
method: Identify impurities using nano-FTIR spectroscopy and high-resolution optical and scanning probe techniques.
Use photo-stress experiments to locate degradation onset at impurity–perovskite interfaces.
Apply machine learning-supported analysis to reflected-light microscopy images for rapid impurity quantification.
evidence_signal: Films with higher impurity density showed accelerated early degradation, while degradation tracking indicated coupled photo- and thermo-chemical contributions.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative detection accuracy or evidence of transferability across different film compositions and manufacturing conditions.
paper_title: High-Throughput Imaging of Degradation-Inducing Microscopic Impurities in Perovskite Solar Cells
